_doc: REQ-435: value that is not in the data. One shared definition read by the backend estimate and the Calculate value dialog. Each driver is a yearly amount from typed assumptions; money inputs use the answer currency; pct inputs are 0-100.

attribution.label: Share of this value the use case earns

inputs.label: Times the task is done per year
inputs.help: How many times a year this task is done across the business, for example 8,000 invoices checked.

inputs.label: People who work on it each time
inputs.help: How many people work on the task each time, for example 2 analysts review every case.

inputs.label: Hours saved each time
inputs.help: Hours of work the use case takes off each time the task is done, for example 1.5 hours saved per case.

inputs.label: Cost of one hour of work
inputs.help: What one hour of a person's time costs the business, salary and overheads together, for example 50 an hour.

inputs.label: People whose work gets faster
inputs.help: How many people do work that the use case makes faster, for example 40 claims handlers.

inputs.label: Cost of one person per year
inputs.help: What one of these people costs the business in a year, salary and overheads together.

inputs.label: Time they get back (%)
inputs.help: The share of their working time they get back each year, from 0 to 100, for example 10 means one day in ten.

inputs.label: Revenue this touches per year
inputs.help: The yearly revenue of the products, customers or sales this use case can influence.

inputs.label: Expected uplift (%)
inputs.help: How much more of that revenue you expect the use case to earn, from 0 to 100, for example 5.

inputs.label: Spend this touches per year
inputs.help: The yearly spend on the cost this use case can reduce, for example what is paid on claims leakage.

inputs.label: Expected cut (%)
inputs.help: How much of that spend you expect the use case to remove, from 0 to 100, for example 10.

inputs.label: Incidents per year today
inputs.help: How many incidents of this kind happen in a year today, for example 120 fraud cases.

inputs.label: Cost of one incident
inputs.help: What one incident costs the business on average, including losses and handling time.

inputs.label: Incidents the use case prevents (%)
inputs.help: The share of those incidents the use case stops, from 0 to 100, for example 30.
